title: Azure Repos and Azure Pipelines
description: Use Azure Repos for version control and understand the structure of a basic Azure Pipelines build.

data.text: Azure Repos is a version control service that hosts Git repositories. Azure Pipelines is the CI/CD engine that builds your code from those repositories. Together they form the backbone of an automated release process.

data.title: Key Repos Features
items: **Unlimited private Git repos** - Free for up to 5 users in the Basic plan
**Pull request policies** - Require reviewers, linked work items, and passing builds before merge
**Branch policies** - Enforce code review, build validation, and comment resolution on specific branches
**File locking** - Prevent conflicting edits to binary files

data.text: An Azure Pipeline is defined in a YAML file (typically azure-pipelines.yml) in the root of your repository. It contains one or more stages, each containing jobs, each containing steps.

data.title: YAML - Minimal Azure Pipeline
data.content: A basic pipeline that runs on every push to main.
data.code:
trigger:
  branches:
    include:
      - main

pool:
  vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'

steps:
  - task: UseDotNet@2
    inputs:
      packageType: 'sdk'
      version: '8.x'

  - script: dotnet build --configuration Release
    displayName: 'Build Solution'

  - script: dotnet test --no-build --verbosity normal
    displayName: 'Run Tests'

data.title: Classic vs YAML Pipelines
data.text: Classic pipelines are configured through a visual editor in the Azure DevOps portal. YAML pipelines live in your repository alongside your code, making them version-controlled and reviewable. Use YAML pipelines for all new projects.

terms.definition: An event that starts a pipeline run. Common triggers are pushes to a branch, pull requests, or scheduled times.
A collection of agents (machines) that run your pipeline jobs. Microsoft-hosted pools provide clean VMs; self-hosted pools use your own machines.
A logical division of a pipeline (e.g., Build, Test, Deploy). Stages can run sequentially or in parallel.

data.title: Exercise: Create Your First Pipeline
data.description: Connect a repo to Azure Pipelines and run a build.
steps: Push a simple .NET or Node.js project to Azure Repos
In Azure DevOps, go to Pipelines > New Pipeline
Add a dotnet test step and save
Run the pipeline and confirm it completes
data.expectedOutcome: A green (successful) pipeline run that builds and tests your code.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Azure Repos hosts private Git repositories with pull request policies
Azure Pipelines are defined in YAML and stored in your repository
A pipeline has stages, jobs, and steps that run on agents
Triggers start pipeline runs automatically on code changes
data.takeaway: Store your pipeline definition in the same repo as your code for full version control.
